summary: 2026-07-27 09:26 AM PDT — The change has three blockers: the planner fingerprint hashes the wrong repository for path-targeted audits, the executability gate accepts thinned L1 schedules, and the report contract accepts an empty “complete” coverage report. Two additional contract/linter mismatches undermine the accepted hybrid-adjudication and OPS-17 drift guarantees. The two deep-audit linters pass, demonstrating that their current phrase checks miss these defects; the full gate could not run because the read-only sandbox prohibited its temporary-directory setup.

findings.title: Planner fingerprint ignores the resolved target
findings.claim: The planner's fp() uses bare `git ls-files`, `git hash-object`, and relative `test -x`, although `/deep-audit [path]` may target a repository other than the current working directory. It therefore fingerprints the caller's repository (or fails outside one), while the engine uses `git -C "$T"` and `$T/$p`. A freshly compiled path-targeted plan can immediately fail AC2, and the two supposedly identical algorithms are not identical.
findings.suggestion: Set `T` to the resolved target root and use the engine's exact `git -C "$T"` / `$T/$p` helper in the planner.

findings.title: Executability gate accepts incomplete standard/deep rows
findings.claim: The loaded-plan check requires only that L1 `unitIds` be drawn from the scope's `codeUnitIds`. A tampered standard/deep row can remove units, reduce `runs`, `estTokens`, and totals consistently, and pass every listed check. The engine will then ledger the row as executed even though part of its scope was skipped. This is weaker than the planner's semantic rule that standard/deep use the full list and light uses the exact every-third sample, enabling the story's prohibited “coverage gap that reads as coverage.”
findings.suggestion: Re-verify exact depth-derived unit resolution: `units = |codeUnitIds|`, standard/deep `unitIds = codeUnitIds`, and light `unitIds` equals the ordered every-third sample; also reject duplicates or order drift.

findings.title: Report schema permits an empty complete report
findings.claim: `ledger`, `coverage.covered`, and `coverage.notCovered` all allow empty arrays while `status` can still be `complete`. A report with no ledger entries and no coverage accounting validates successfully, contrary to AC6's mandatory per-row ledger/non-empty coverage account and AC7's prohibition on presenting a partial or absent sweep as complete.
findings.suggestion: Require a non-empty ledger and at least one coverage entry, then add a report semantic check that ledger identities exactly equal plan-row identities, coverage is derived from ledger state, and per-row verified counts equal the findings.

findings.title: Evidence schema still claims blanket-deterministic adjudication
findings.claim: The schema says a “separate deterministic adjudication step” scores evidence, contradicting the accepted AR-2 contract: only the mechanical tier is deterministic, while unresolved cases go through explicitly non-deterministic model judgment. This leaves the schema describing the rejected design rather than the skill's implemented rules.
findings.suggestion: Replace the blanket-deterministic statement with a reference to SKILL.md's two-tier adjudication contract, without restating the rule.

findings.title: Drift linter enforces duplicated schema prose
findings.claim: Despite lines 8–9 and AC10 requiring each rule to be pinned once in the skill and schema descriptions merely to reference it, these checks require the evidence schema to repeat claim-blindness, claim exclusion, and default-refute wording; lines 142–145 likewise require report-rule prose. This duplication already allowed the contradictory deterministic-adjudication text to pass while the linter reported 96/96 checks green.
findings.suggestion: Pin behavioral wording only in SKILL.md. For schemas, check structural constraints plus a concise SKILL.md reference, and add `absent` checks for duplicated load-bearing prose.
